questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must stop completely at the marked stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions right ahead. This sign warns drivers about an upcoming right curve.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive with caution, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on roads near schools. It warns drivers to slow down, be careful, and watch for children.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road surface. To prevent hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Decrease your speed.
Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed.
questions.explanation: In rainy weather, slow down to reduce hydroplaning risk. Driving too fast can cause tires to ride up on water and lose contact with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and maintain your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, signs warn you about workers, slow-moving equipment, and closed lanes. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions are more likely when one vehicle moves faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster than traffic increases collision risk. Driving slower than traffic also causes danger because other vehicles may hit you or swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: Where should drivers be particularly alert to children?

options.text: School zones and playgrounds
Residential neighborhoods
All of the above locations

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above locations
questions.explanation: Use extreme caution wherever children are present. Be alert around schools and playgrounds. Also be careful in neighborhoods where children may play in the streets.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should be driving:

options.text: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
More slowly than the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter a freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:

options.text: Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.
Passing is permitted when it's safe.
Passing is not permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted when it's safe.
questions.explanation: Dashed yellow lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: When driving on a slippery surface, such as snow or ice:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Maintain traction by following other vehicles closely.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: To prevent skidding on slippery surfaces, shift to a low gear before going down steep hills. Also follow the vehicle in front of you at a greater distance than normal. Avoid quick stops. Unless you have antilock brakes, pump the brakes to slow or stop.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of the road mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double yellow centerline means no one can cross it to pass another vehicle, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead, such as curves, steep hills, or other dangerous conditions. You need to be ready to act.

questions.question: When making a left turn, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Signal to other drivers.
Cut the corner.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cut the corner.
questions.explanation: Signal and slow down at least 100 feet before turning left. Do not cut the corner short, as this can interfere with other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a broken traffic signal?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Stop completely, look, and yield the right-of-way before entering.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and nerves. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that affects your driving, whether it is legal or illegal.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the road.
Turn back onto the road immediately.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then gradually return to the road.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road immediately. Reduce your speed, check for traffic, and gradually turn back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: At what speed can your car start to hydroplane on wet roads?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: At speeds up to 35 mph, tires can move water away from the tire. Once you go faster than 35 mph, tires lose this ability. Your tires may lose contact with the road and ride over water like water skis.

questions.question: When should you not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red?

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Even if the light is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can fully cross before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Watch for a second train even after the first one passes. Do not proceed until all gates are raised and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: An oncoming driver has high beams on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show your blind spots. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see these areas clearly.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Find a large enough gap to safely enter traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless you cannot find a safe gap to merge.

questions.question: What do drivers need to do on interstate highways?

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: Why is night driving more dangerous than daytime driving?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: Low visibility and headlight glare make it harder to see ahead at night. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, what should you do?

options.text: Slightly increase your speed.
Expect the unexpected.
Expect construction workers to yield to cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected hazards. Drive with extra caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and workers.

questions.question: Who can drivers be required to obey?

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers with broken-down vehicles on the road.
Flaggers at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: Drivers must obey flaggers' instructions and signals. They are there to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This lets other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians know your plans.

questions.question: A police officer directs you to go through a red traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Police officer instructions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's directions.

questions.question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
When parked on a level roadway with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight to prevent veering into oncoming traffic if hit from behind. On hills, turn your wheels to prevent rolling into traffic if brakes fail.

questions.question: When must you use your low beams?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off precipitation and make glare worse, reducing visibility. Some vehicles have fog lights for additional visibility.
